spec.question: Can a learned qualified whole become a reusable operational unit that expands lawful reachability under a fixed composition budget, rather than merely being a cache?
spec.incumbent: Existing qualification/composition owners can promote a learned whole into a reusable unit; under a fixed bounded composition grammar this can make a later target reachable without granting new authority.
spec.rival: Any apparent expansion is only search caching/compression; the target was already reachable from primitives under the same lawful budget or the macro smuggles a supplied sequence.
spec.manipulation: Use primitives A,B,C and a fixed composition depth/budget of 2. Train/qualify learned whole M=(A then B) from actual experience without supplying M as a macro. Later target requires (M then C). Test before M, after M, with M withheld, and with primitive search budget increased to 3 as an oracle comparison.
spec.incumbent_prediction: Target is unreachable at fixed depth before M, reachable after M as a qualified unit, unreachable when M is withheld/stale, while a depth-3 primitive oracle confirms the underlying sequence existed but exceeded the fixed lawful budget.
spec.rival_prediction: Target is reachable at fixed depth before M, or remains reachable when M is withheld, or M only works because its sequence was supplied rather than learned.
spec.measurement: Reachability proof/search trace, composition depth, qualified unit identity/dependencies, target success, behavior after M staleness.
spec.minimal_embodiment: Research-only bounded composition fixture around existing learned-whole/qualification owners; claim ceiling explicitly limited to fixed-budget reachability expansion.
spec.falsifier: No reversible dependence of fixed-budget reachability on the learned qualified whole.
spec.loop_plus: If positive, test whether the new whole can itself participate in another learning level before any recursive-closure claim.
